reason: the underlying MCP client request was still pending when Code Mode returned its timeout error; the underlying MCP client request was still pending after a 1500ms bounded observation period; the withheld late response still fulfilled the abandoned MCP client request; no notifications/cancelled was emitted by the integration

observation_notes.sdk_cancellation_trigger: MCP SDK 1.32.2 Protocol.request sends notifications/cancelled only when an AbortSignal aborts or its own request timeout fires; the M2 adapter passes no options or signal.
observation_notes.server_side_operation_state_at_withhold: The genuine upstream server had already returned its response before withholding; this experiment measures the client/transport boundary, not server-side cancellation of executing tool code.

limitations: One fault phase per run at the transport-response boundary; no server-side cancellation of executing code is proven.
The withheld response is released by the harness after measurement; that release is the late-completion probe, not cleanup.
The 60s MCP SDK default request timeout is deliberately not exercised, so a cancellation at 60s would not be attributable to Code Mode.
No production implementation, S1-A2, ADR-034 M4, enforcement, performance, or closure claim is made.
smallest_correction_boundary: Host-call boundary only: the adapter/executor bridge would need to propagate an AbortSignal (or equivalent cancellation token) from QuickJS timeout cleanup into client.callTool(), then await transport-level settlement. No server-side cancellation of already-executing tool code is implied.
